subject: Day 5: weight nadir; six wet diapers expected; cord stump
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 5. The weight nadir resolves today or tomorrow — most term infants begin gaining 0.5-1 oz per day from this point. Bilirubin starts trending down. Target output by today: at least six wet diapers and three or more stools. The cord stump may start drying meaningfully; do not pull it.

Action items
- If the first-week pediatrician visit has not yet happened, call this morning. Five days is the outer edge of the recommended window. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Keep the cord stump dry. Sponge baths only until it falls off (typically day 5-15). Do not apply alcohol or other products. AAP HealthyChildren on cord care: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/bathing-skin-care/Pages/default.aspx
- Continue the feeding log; you will hand it to the pediatrician at the next visit.
- If you have not yet filed Avi's birth certificate or SS-5 application, do it today. SSA application: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/
- Order another 2-3 weeks of newborn-size diapers if you are running low. Most newborns outgrow newborn-size somewhere between week 3-5 — do not over-buy.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump drying, occasional small bloodspot at the base. Mustard-yellow or tan stool. Faint baby acne or milia. Bilirubin trending down today.
- [low concern] Weight gain has not yet started visibly — this is normal until day 5-7.
- [monitor] Cord stump weeping or surrounding skin slightly red without spreading.
- [call within 24h] Pus, foul smell, or redness extending more than 1 cm around the cord (omphalitis is rare but emergent). Yellow tinge on legs or below. Fewer than six wet diapers today. Weight loss greater than 10% of birth weight.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Tummy time on a parent's chest for 2-5 minutes at a time after a feed when Avi is alert. He will lift his head briefly or turn it side-to-side. This counter-positions the natural side-preference that develops when newborns spend most time supine. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 7-10: weight check; most regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Further reading
- AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time and back-to-sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- AAP HealthyChildren on bathing and skin care: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/bathing-skin-care/Pages/default.aspx
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp — the 5 S's for soothing: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-based decisions: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
